title.en: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body

text.en: Ravi opens his lunch box and finds roti, dal, vegetables and a banana. Which part gives him energy, which helps him grow and which keeps him healthy? Let us look at food closely.

Different regions of India have different foods, but all of them come from plants or animals. Food gives us energy, helps us grow and repair our bodies and keeps us healthy.
The main components are carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water. Carbohydrates, such as in rice and roti, give energy. Proteins, in dal, eggs and milk, help growth and repair. Fats, in ghee and oil, give a lot of energy. Vitamins and minerals protect us from diseases. Fibre helps digestion and water keeps the body working.
Iodine solution turns blue-black when starch is present. A paper rubbed with a food that contains fat shows an oily patch that stays when dry. Testing helps us find what a food contains.
A balanced diet has all the components in the right amount. Not eating enough of something causes deficiency diseases. For example lack of vitamin C can cause bleeding gums, and lack of iron causes weakness. Eating too much junk food can lead to being overweight.
Millets such as ragi and jowar are cereals rich in nutrients that grow with little water. Food miles are the distance food travels from farm to plate. Local food has fewer food miles and is often fresher.
Eat slowly, chew well, avoid wasting food and wash your hands before eating. Choose fresh and home cooked meals and drink enough water.

problem.en: Which food group does dal belong to?

text.en: Dal is rich in protein.
So it is a protein food.

prompt.en: Explain why a balanced diet is better than eating only one kind of food.

requiredIdeas.en: One food cannot give them all.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking only energy foods are needed.

points.en: Food gives energy, growth and protection.
Carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre, water.
Millets and local foods are good choices.
